source.titleEnglishInternal: Explain Media or Entera at a Seville Tostada Bar
source.objectiveEnglishInternal: Explain how tostadas are ordered by bread type, size and topping, and why locals choose each one.
source.speakingEnglishInternal: You are explaining Seville's tostada system to the AI, hostel roommate Ingrid: walk her through bread type, size and toppings and why locals choose each, using impersonal se (se pide media o entera) and si + present (si pides mollete…).

readerVerbExamples.target: Aquí se pide media o entera.
readerVerbExamples.native: Here you order a half or a whole.

readerVerbExamples.target: Si tienes mucha hambre, pide una entera.
readerVerbExamples.native: If you're really hungry, order a whole one.

readerVerbExamples.target: Mucha gente prefiere el pan de viena.
readerVerbExamples.native: A lot of people prefer the Vienna roll.

readerVerbExamples.target: Si no comes cerdo, evita la manteca colorá.
readerVerbExamples.native: If you don't eat pork, avoid the manteca colorá.

readerVerbExamples.target: Le explico a Ingrid cómo se piden las tostadas.
readerVerbExamples.native: I explain to Ingrid how tostadas are ordered.

archivedDraft.scene: A traveler helps a friend understand a café’s bread menu without assuming ingredients.

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: Aquí se pide media o entera, según el hambre que tengas.
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: Here you order a half or a whole, depending on how hungry you are.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: ここでは、おなかの空き具合に合わせて、メディア（半分）かエンテラ（丸ごと）を頼むんだよ。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Here you order a half or a whole, depending on how hungry you are.

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: Si pides mollete, el pan queda tierno por dentro.
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: If you order a mollete, the bread stays soft inside.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: モジェテを頼むと、パンの中はやわらかいままだよ。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: If you order a mollete, the bread stays soft inside.

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: Si tienes mucha hambre, pide una entera.
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: If you're really hungry, order a whole one.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: すごくおなかが空いているなら、エンテラを頼んでね。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: If you're really hungry, order a whole one.

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: Si no comes cerdo, evita la manteca colorá y la zurrapa.
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: If you don't eat pork, avoid the manteca colorá and the zurrapa.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: 豚肉を食べないなら、マンテカ・コロラとスラパは避けてね。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: If you don't eat pork, avoid the manteca colorá and the zurrapa.

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: Perdone, ¿el pan de la casa es mollete o de viena?
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: Excuse me, is the house bread a mollete or a Vienna roll?
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: すみません、お店のパンはモジェテですか、それともパン・デ・ビエナですか。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Excuse me, is the house bread a mollete or a Vienna roll?

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: Gracias por corregirme, no lo sabía.
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: Thanks for correcting me, I didn't know that.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: 訂正してくださってありがとうございます。知りませんでした。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Thanks for correcting me, I didn't know that.

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: Para mí, media de tomate con aceite, por favor.
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: For me, a half with tomato and oil, please.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: 私は、トマトとオイルのメディア（半分）をお願いします。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: For me, a half with tomato and oil, please.

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: ¿Cómo se pide aquí si la quiero poco tostada?
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: How do you order it here if I want it lightly toasted?
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: 軽めに焼いてほしいときは、ここではどう頼めばいいですか。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: How do you order it here if I want it lightly toasted?

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Esta mañana, en un bar de tostadas de Triana, le explico a Ingrid cómo se piden las tostadas en Sevilla.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: This morning, at a tostada bar in Triana, I explain to Ingrid how tostadas are ordered in Seville.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 今朝、トリアナにあるトスターダ（トースト）のバルで、セビリアでのトスターダの頼み方をイングリッドに説明します。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: This morning, at a tostada bar in Triana, I explain to Ingrid how tostadas are ordered in Seville.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Yo: Aquí se pide primero el pan y luego lo que lleva encima.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Me: Here you order the bread first and then the topping.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 私：ここでは、先にパンを頼んで、そのあと上にのせるものを頼むんだよ。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Me: Here you order the bread first and then the topping.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Yo: Aquí se pide media o entera, según el hambre que tengas.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Me: Here you order a half or a whole, depending on how hungry you are.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 私：ここでは、おなかの空き具合に合わせて、メディア（半分）かエンテラ（丸ごと）を頼むんだよ。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Me: Here you order a half or a whole, depending on how hungry you are.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Yo: Si tienes mucha hambre, pide una entera.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Me: If you're really hungry, order a whole one.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 私：すごくおなかが空いているなら、エンテラを頼んでね。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Me: If you're really hungry, order a whole one.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Yo: Si pides mollete, el pan queda tierno por dentro, porque tiene mucha miga.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Me: If you order a mollete, the bread stays soft inside, because it has a lot of soft crumb.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 私：モジェテを頼むと、パンの中はやわらかいままだよ。中身（ミガ）がたっぷりあるからね。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Me: If you order a mollete, the bread stays soft inside, because it has a lot of soft crumb.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Yo: El pan de viena tiene la corteza más fina y crujiente, y mucha gente lo prefiere por eso.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Me: The Vienna roll has a thinner, crunchier crust, and a lot of people prefer it for that reason.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 私：パン・デ・ビエナのほうが皮が薄くてカリッとしているから、そっちを好む人が多いんだ。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Me: The Vienna roll has a thinner, crunchier crust, and a lot of people prefer it for that reason.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Yo: Si pides pitufo, te traen un pan más pequeño, perfecto para acompañar un café.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Me: If you order a pitufo, they bring you a smaller roll, perfect to go with a coffee.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 私：ピトゥフォを頼むと、小さめのパンが出てくるよ。コーヒーのお供にぴったりだよ。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Me: If you order a pitufo, they bring you a smaller roll, perfect to go with a coffee.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Yo: Creo que el pan de la casa es mollete, pero voy a preguntar.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Me: I think the house bread is a mollete, but I'm going to ask.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 私：お店のパンはモジェテだと思うけど、聞いてみるね。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Me: I think the house bread is a mollete, but I'm going to ask.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Le digo a la dueña: Perdone, ¿el pan de la casa es mollete o de viena?
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: I say to the owner: Excuse me, is the house bread a mollete or a Vienna roll?
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 私は店主の女性に言います。「すみません、お店のパンはモジェテですか、それともパン・デ・ビエナですか。」
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: I say to the owner: Excuse me, is the house bread a mollete or a Vienna roll?

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Rocío: El pan de la casa es de viena, y el mollete se pide aparte.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Rocío: The house bread is a Vienna roll, and the mollete is ordered separately.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: ロシオ：うちのパンはパン・デ・ビエナで、モジェテは別注文になります。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Rocío: The house bread is a Vienna roll, and the mollete is ordered separately.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Yo: Gracias por corregirme, no lo sabía.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Me: Thanks for correcting me, I didn't know that.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 私：訂正してくださってありがとうございます。知りませんでした。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Me: Thanks for correcting me, I didn't know that.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Luego le cuento a Ingrid que lo más típico es el tomate rallado con un buen chorro de aceite de oliva, porque es ligero y fresco.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Then I tell Ingrid that the most typical choice is grated tomato with a good drizzle of olive oil, because it is light and fresh.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: それからイングリッドに、いちばんの定番はすりおろしトマトにオリーブオイルをたっぷりかけたもので、軽くてさっぱりしているからだと話します。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Then I tell Ingrid that the most typical choice is grated tomato with a good drizzle of olive oil, because it is light and fresh.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Yo: La manteca colorá es manteca de cerdo con pimentón, y la zurrapa de lomo lleva trocitos de lomo en manteca.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Me: Manteca colorá is pork lard with paprika, and zurrapa de lomo has little pieces of pork loin in lard.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 私：マンテカ・コロラはパプリカ（ピメントン）入りの豚のラードで、スラパ・デ・ロモはラードの中に豚ロースの小さなかけらが入っているんだ。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Me: Manteca colorá is pork lard with paprika, and zurrapa de lomo has little pieces of pork loin in lard.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Ingrid me dice que no come cerdo, y le explico que el jamón serrano también es de cerdo.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Ingrid tells me she doesn't eat pork, and I explain that cured ham is pork too.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: イングリッドが豚肉は食べないと言い、私は生ハムも豚肉だと説明します。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Ingrid tells me she doesn't eat pork, and I explain that cured ham is pork too.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Yo: Si no comes cerdo, evita la manteca colorá y la zurrapa.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Me: If you don't eat pork, avoid the manteca colorá and the zurrapa.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 私：豚肉を食べないなら、マンテカ・コロラとスラパは避けてね。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Me: If you don't eat pork, avoid the manteca colorá and the zurrapa.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Ingrid: ¿Cómo se pide aquí si la quiero poco tostada?
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Ingrid: How do you order it here if I want it lightly toasted?
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: イングリッド：軽めに焼いてほしいときは、ここではどう頼めばいいですか。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Ingrid: How do you order it here if I want it lightly toasted?

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Rocío: Se pide con poco tueste, y se la sacamos más blandita.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Rocío: You order it with light toasting, and we bring it out to you softer.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: ロシオ：「軽めの焼き加減で」と頼んでいただければ、少しやわらかめにしてお出しします。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Rocío: You order it with light toasting, and we bring it out to you softer.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Al final, Ingrid pide media de tomate con aceite y poco tueste, y Rocío le deja el salero en la mesa.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: In the end, Ingrid orders a half with tomato and oil, lightly toasted, and Rocío leaves the salt shaker on the table for her.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 最後に、イングリッドはトマトとオイルのメディア（半分）を軽めの焼き加減で注文し、ロシオはテーブルに塩入れを置いていってくれます。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: In the end, Ingrid orders a half with tomato and oil, lightly toasted, and Rocío leaves the salt shaker on the table for her.

japaneseSpecificFocusCandidate: Explain Seville tostada bread, size, topping and pork ingredients to Ingrid, correct the house-bread assumption with owner Rocío, then order lightly toasted half tomato and oil.
speakingGoalInternal: You are explaining Seville's tostada system to the AI, hostel roommate Ingrid: walk her through bread type, size and toppings and why locals choose each, using impersonal se (se pide media o entera) and si + present (si pides mollete…).
speakingGoalJapaneseDraft: AIが演じるホステルのルームメイト、イングリッドに、セビリアのトスターダ（トースト）の頼み方を説明しましょう。パンの種類、サイズ、トッピングを順に案内し、地元の人がそれぞれを選ぶ理由も伝えます。スペイン語の非人称 se（se pide media o entera）と si＋現在形（si pides mollete…）の出典上の焦点は、追加の日本語文法指導として未承認です。
sourceConflictInternal: Current 18-turn source takes a Triana teach-back through half/whole, mollete, Vienna roll, pitufo and toppings; owner Rocío corrects the house-bread assumption, Ingrid avoids pork, then orders a lightly toasted half with tomato and oil. Archived generic 10-turn scene omits these named breads, pork-ingredient distinctions, correction and final order; it remains separate evidence, not a replacement or migration source.

reviewQuestionsInternal: Qualified Japanese, Andalusian food, pork-ingredient, locale and contextual dictionary review remains open; this packet is unapproved and not learner-visible.
The source teaches Spanish impersonal se and si + present; Japanese renders the communicative purpose rather than claiming a direct grammar equivalent.
Media and entera are Spanish size names. Candidate Japanese uses メディア（半分） and エンテラ; a Japanese reviewer should check transliteration and first-use support.
Mollete, pan de viena, pitufo, manteca colorá and zurrapa de lomo require Andalusian food-name and Japanese transliteration review. The draft uses モジェテ, パン・デ・ビエナ, ピトゥフォ, マンテカ・コロラ and スラパ・デ・ロモ.
The pork-lard spreads and jamón serrano remain explicitly pork. 生ハム is a draft Japanese equivalent for cured ham; dictionary context still needs review.
Rocío is the female café owner; Ingrid is the hostel roommate. The house bread is corrected to pan de viena, and mollete is ordered separately. Japanese guest/owner register needs fluent review.
Tostada can imply another dish in Japanese. A first-use トースト gloss is a draft teaching aid, not a qualified terminology decision.
